To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

camptothecins (CPTs) were incorporated into polymeric micelles with high efficiency and stability using block copolymer possessing high contents of hydrophobic moities such as benzyl and methyl naphthyl ester groups.

the evaporation method brought out high CPT incorporation yields and stability in polymeric micelles with hydrophobic blocks possessing high contents of ester groups, indicating that the molecular design of the inner core forming hydrophobic blocks and the incorporation method are important for obtaining targeting using polymeric carriers.
the incorporation efficiency of CPT to the polymeric micelle system was improved by the molecular design of hydrophobic block and the drug incorporation method.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of polymeric micelles for targeting and the drug incorporation method.
the design of polymeric micelle systems for the incorporation of a water-insoluble anticancer agent, camptothein (CPT).
the development of polymeric micelle drug carrier systems for water-insoluble anticancer agents such as camptothecins.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the incorporation method and the hydrophobic chain design of the block copolymerable polymer are the two most critical factors in the design and fabrication of a polymeric micellar system containing water-insoluble drugs such as CPT.
the evaporation method was superior to the dialysis and emulsion methods for the CPT incorporation to polymeric micelle systems.

a water-insoluble drug, CPT, was successfully incorporated into a polymeric micellar carrier system using an evaporation method and the resultant polymeric micelles showed good stability and targeting ability.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a polymeric micellar carrier system can be a useful carrier of water-insoluble anticancer agents, and that the incorporation efficiency and stability of the carrier system can be improved by the combination of molecular design of polymeric micellar components and drug incorporation methods.

the polymeric micelle system containing CPT can be prepared in high yields with high stability by the evaporation method using poly(ethylene glycols)-poly(aspartic acid) block copolymer having high contents of benzylester and methylnaphthylester moieties as the hydrophobic moities.

the polymeric micelles prepared from block copolymerable possessing high contents of methylnapthyl ester group as hydrophobic blocks were most suitable for the CPT incorporation by the evaporation method.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the evaporation method is a useful incorporation technique to prepare polymeric micelles with high drug-loading efficiency, and that the chemical structure of the hydrophobes is a key parameter to control the drug release from polymeric micelles.
the evaporation method is an effective method for the incorporation of water-insoluble drugs into polymeric micelles.

the evaporation method is a promising method for incorporation of water-insoluble drugs into polymeric micelle drug carriers, and the incorporation efficiency is highly dependent on the chemical structure of the hydrophobically modified block copolymar.
